text.p: Glasgow Rangers' ambitions of being regarded as one of the biggest clubs in Europe were boosted on Wednesday when a single financier invested 40 million pounds ($66.1 million) in the club.

Rangers, whose dreams of European glory have been thwarted by poor performances in the European Champions' League over the past four seasons, announced that a Bahamas-based company, Albancy Inc, which is wholly owned by financier Joe Lewis, had bought a 25 per cent stake in the club.

In a statement, Rangers said the club was now worth 160 million pounds ($264.6 million) and that the money invested on Wednesday would be used to "strengthen playing resources, commence a hotel and leisure development adjacent to the Rangers stadium, establish a new player development centre and training facilities, and repay bank borrowings."
The deal does not affect the position of Rangers chairman David Murray who retains his controlling interest at Ibrox.
The deal will be organised through the English National Investment Company (ENIC).
The Rangers statement said the soccer industry in Britain was undergoing significant changes.

"In particular, the impact of the Bosman ruling on wage and transfer fee levels, increasing revenue flow from television -- including a possible move to pay per view -- and the expected expansion of European competitions have led to considerable speculation as to the potential value of football clubs.
"The boards of ENIC and Rangers believe that the new capital will assist Rangers in its plans to consolidate its position as a leading European club."
The statement added that Rangers would, in due, course, expect to be floated on the London Stock Exchange."
Rangers are currently top of the Scottish premier division and are bidding for their ninth successive title. That would equal the record set by their arch-rivals Celtics in the 1960s and 70s.
